products.name: DoorDash
products.key_insight: DoorDash's behavioral design reveals a fundamental tension in on-demand platforms: the features that make the user experience feel urgent and seamless (countdown timers, pre-selected tips, one-tap reorder) are the same features that obscure true costs and reduce deliberative decision-making. DoorDash charges a delivery fee, a service fee, a small order fee, and applies dynamic pricing — but the total only appears at checkout, after the user has invested time browsing menus and customizing orders (sunk cost). The DashPass subscription ($9.99/month) transforms occasional delivery into a committed habit by making each marginal order feel 'free.' DoorDash is a masterclass in how to design for habitual, low-friction purchasing — and a cautionary tale about what that means for consumer spending.
products.top_technique: Delivery Time Countdown as Urgency Commitment
